question.text: Saraswati Growth Fund is a SEBI-registered Category II AIF set up as a contributory, determinate, irrevocable trust. In FY25, the fund earns INR 80 crore of dividend and interest and INR 25 crore categorised (post Finance Act 2025) as capital gains on transfer of unlisted equity. From the MANAGER's perspective, which statement best describes the fund-level tax treatment of these two income streams under Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) of the ITA?

answer.text: Both income streams are taxed at the fund level at MMR because AIFs do not enjoy pass-through.
Both income streams are exempt in the fund's hands and chargeable directly to the unit-holders in the same character in which they arose.
Dividend/interest is exempt at the fund; capital gains are taxed at the fund at 12.5%.
Only dividends enjoy pass-through; interest and capital gains are taxed at the fund at MMR.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 115UB read with Section 10(23FBA) gives Cat I and Cat II AIFs tax pass-through status for ALL income OTHER than business income. Dividend, interest and capital gains flow through to unit-holders in the same character in which the fund earned them. Post Finance Act 2025, securities held by Cat I/II AIFs are expressly capital assets under Section 2(14) — so the INR 25 cr is capital gains that passes through. **The Trap:** Option A confuses Cat III (fund-level tax) with Cat I/II. Option C invents a fund-level cap gains charge that does not exist for pass-through funds. Option D wrongly splits the streams — pass-through is uniform across all non-business income heads. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A frames this from the distributor's client-KYC angle. XIX-C expects the manager to structure PPM distribution waterfalls consistent with Section 115UB and issue Form 64C to LPs by 30 June each year. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In the PPM, flag expressly that the fund is a 'pass-through' vehicle under Section 115UB so LPs know each head of income retains character in their hands — vital for corporates claiming Section 80M dividend deduction and individuals using the LTCG INR 1.25 lakh exemption.
